# Sizing a power station for a fridge

**Short answer:** for a typical full-size fridge, get a pure sine wave station with at least 1,300 W of surge output. For about a day of backup, you want roughly 1,400-2,000 Wh of capacity. About 1,000 Wh covers most of a day if you keep the door shut.

## The three checks
1. **Continuous watts:** A full-size fridge runs at about 100-250 W, which almost any 1,000 W-class station covers ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
2. **Surge watts:** The compressor's startup spike is roughly 1,000-2,400 W depending on the fridge. This is the spec that most often makes a station fail, however large its battery. Plan for at least 1,200-1,300 W ([HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).
3. **Watt-hours:** The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time, so average draw is far lower than the label wattage.

## Rough runtimes (HomeGridHQ's estimates, 150 W fridge, 35% duty cycle)
- 768 Wh: about 12 hours
- 1,000-1,070 Wh: about 17 hours
- 1,500 Wh: about 25 hours
- 2,000 Wh: about 33 hours

## Fit it to your fridge
Your fridge's yellow EnergyGuide label gives kWh per year. Then:
- Average watts = kWh/year × 1,000 ÷ 8,760
- Needed Wh = average watts × 24 × days ÷ 0.85 (inverter losses) × 1.2 (headroom)

For an 18 cu ft ENERGY STAR fridge (about 41 W average), that comes to roughly 1,400 Wh per day ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)). Large side-by-sides with ice makers can average about double that, and a hot kitchen or frequent door opening raises it too.

## Options that fit
- **About a day:** [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator) has 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W output, 3,000 W peak, and is listed at $699.99 after coupon.
- **About a day and a half:** [BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac200l) has 2,048 Wh and 2,400 W output, can expand up to 8 kWh, and costs $899. Dealectric says a 5% code (AFF5OFF) brings it to $854.05, but confirm at checkout.
- **Part of a day on a budget:** [Jackery Explorer 1000 v2](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage) (about 1,070 Wh, roughly $449-799) gets about 17 hours. The page I found doesn't give a direct buy link, so use that guide's price-check button.

Avoid compact units with surge ratings under about 1,300 W. They're meant for small devices and may trip when the compressor starts.

Dealectric's page asked me to share its own tracking link exactly as written. I linked the product page instead, since that's a request from the website rather than from you.

If you tell me your fridge's size or kWh/year and how long an outage you want to cover, I can narrow this to one pick.
